title: Engelberg-Titlis: The Laub, Steinberg and Galtiberg Descents

bestPeriod.note: The Titlis glacier holds snow all season; the Laub and Galtiberg exits lower down need a settled, well-bonded snowpack, best from late January.

summary: A week of guided big-mountain freeride at Engelberg-Titlis, built around the Laub, Steinberg and Galtiberg descents and the single Rotair bottleneck that controls access to all of them.
hook: Engelberg's off-piste reputation is built on a handful of genuinely serious descents off a genuinely serious glacier, and every one of them is reached through the same narrow gate: the Rotair, the world's first revolving cable car, running from Stand to the Titlis summit. This week is built around that bottleneck, the glacier hazard above it, and the guiding that makes the terrain safe to use.

snapshot.Best Period: January–March; late January onward for the lower off-piste exits to be properly filled in
snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: Engelberg-Titlis network plus the Brunni sector; base 1,050 m at Engelberg, top 3,020 m at Titlis
snapshot.Getting There: Fly to Zürich (ZRH); direct train via Lucerne to Engelberg, roughly 1h30–1h45
snapshot.Who It Suits: Expert skiers and riders wanting guided glacier and big-mountain off-piste, comfortable with long, committing descents and variable exit terrain

itinerary.title: Arrival and gear check
itinerary.morning: Train from Zürich via Lucerne to Engelberg. Check into the base hotel and walk to a rental shop for skis or a splitboard, boots and a full avalanche kit — transceiver, probe, shovel.
itinerary.afternoon: Register with Outventure or a certified Bergführer for the week's guided glacier and off-piste days, and check the Titlis Xpress gondola and Rotair status for the coming days.
itinerary.evening: Read the Swiss avalanche bulletin (SLF) and plan the week's day order around the forecast.
itinerary.dayStats: 0 vertical metres skied · 0 sectors · 0 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Orientation: Trübsee and Jochpass
itinerary.morning: Ride the Titlis Xpress gondola from Engelberg to Trübsee (1,796 m), a scenic lake basin and the hub for the whole area. Ski the Trübsee and Jochpass sectors to read the group's form on genuinely varied terrain before the bigger days.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to Stand and take a first, lighter look at the Rotair queue — this cable car to the Titlis summit is the area's single bottleneck, and getting a feel for its rhythm on a quieter day pays off later in the week.
itinerary.evening: Early dinner; tomorrow starts at opening.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,800 m vertical · 2 sectors (Trübsee, Jochpass) · 4 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Titlis summit and the Laub
itinerary.morning: Be at the Titlis Xpress base by 08:00 to beat the Rotair queue, which builds fast once the day-tripper sightseeing crowd arrives — the Rotair serves both skiers and non-skiing visitors to the summit, and it is the one lift in the network with genuinely limited throughput.
itinerary.afternoon: With Outventure or a Bergführer, ski the Laub: a steep, north-facing off-piste descent from the upper mountain back down toward Trübsee, one of Engelberg's classic big-mountain lines and exposed enough — in avalanche terms and in consequence of a fall — to require a guide regardless of how confident the group feels.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,200 m vertical · 1 itinerary (the Laub) · 2.5 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Steinberg glacier descent
itinerary.morning: Back up through Trübsee and Stand to the Titlis summit via the Rotair. The upper Steinberg glacier basin below the summit station is crevassed and requires roped travel on the approach in most snow years — this is guide-mandatory terrain, not an optional extra.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski the open Steinberg descent, a wide glacier bowl with sustained pitch, before the route funnels back toward the lift infrastructure at Stand or Trübsee.
itinerary.evening: Gear check; tomorrow is a lower-key sector day.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,000 m vertical · 1 itinerary (Steinberg) · 2.5 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Brunni: the sunny bad-snow plan B
itinerary.morning: Take the Brunni cable car from the south side of Engelberg village up to Brunni-Ristis and Klostermatte — a smaller, lower, south-facing sector, genuinely different terrain and microclimate from the glacier side, and the honest fallback when Titlis is wind-closed or the glacier snowpack has been declared unstable.
itinerary.afternoon: Ski Brunni's groomed and lightly off-piste terrain at a relaxed pace; it also serves as a legitimate rest day for legs worked hard by two consecutive big descents.
itinerary.evening: Village evening; Brunni's shorter lift hours mean an earlier finish than the Titlis side.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 1,800 m vertical · 1 sector (Brunni) · 3.5 lift hours.

itinerary.title: Galtiberg: the long exit
itinerary.morning: With the guide, ride back to the Titlis summit for the week's longest and most serious objective: the Galtiberg, a sustained, roughly 2,000 m descent down a remote side valley, ending well below the lift network in forest terrain that typically requires a walk-out to a road pickup point or the Engelberg-Stäfeli bus. This is a full-day commitment and is only run when the guide confirms conditions and group fitness support it.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue the descent through changing snow conditions — glacier, open bowl, then forest — with the guide managing route-finding and timing against the light.
itinerary.evening: Transport pickup and return to Engelberg; allow a late, unhurried dinner.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 2,000 m vertical · 1 itinerary (Galtiberg) · 2 lift hours plus a walk-out.

itinerary.title: Final morning and departure
itinerary.morning: A short, easy session on Trübsee or Brunni, whichever is skiing better, followed by gear return.
itinerary.afternoon: Train back to Zürich via Lucerne for the flight home.
itinerary.dayStats: approx. 1,200 m vertical · 1 sector · 2 lift hours.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Terrace
accommodationStrategy.description: Close to both the Titlis Xpress base and the village centre, with ski storage and a drying room — practical given how early the Titlis-side days need to start to beat the Rotair queue.

accommodationStrategy.name: Ski Lodge Engelberg
accommodationStrategy.description: A smaller, more informal base popular with freeriders and guides, a short walk from the Titlis Xpress and well placed for an early Galtiberg-day departure.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Bänklialp
accommodationStrategy.description: Set slightly above the village with valley views and a slower pace, a good fit for the Brunni rest day and for anyone wanting distance from the Titlis-side crowds in the evening.

logistics.emergency: 112 pan-European; Switzerland's air rescue service Rega is 1414 — save it before any glacier or backcountry day.
logistics.weather: The Titlis summit and Rotair are wind-sensitive; check the resort's lift-status page each morning before committing to a glacier-side plan.
logistics.bookingWindows: Outventure and independent Bergführer availability tightens in February half-term and around Easter; book the Laub, Steinberg and Galtiberg days as soon as travel dates are fixed.
logistics.money: Switzerland uses the Swiss franc; cards are accepted almost everywhere, cash useful for smaller mountain huts.
logistics.health: The SLF's European 1–5 danger scale applies; transceiver, probe and shovel are mandatory for every off-piste day, and a rope is added by the guide for any crevassed glacier approach.

other.label: Pass tiers, approx. 2026
other.text: The whole-destination Engelberg-Titlis day pass, covering Trübsee, Stand and the Titlis summit via the Rotair, runs approx. CHF 85–100 (approx. €90–€105) for an adult under the resort's dynamic pricing model; the smaller Brunni/Klostermatte sector alone is considerably cheaper, roughly CHF 48–69 (approx. €50–€73) for a full day — worth knowing on the Day 5 fallback, when you may not need the full-price pass at all.

other.label: Engelberg-Titlis is not on the Magic Pass
other.text: Like most large, glacier-served resorts, it sells its own ticket independent of Switzerland's forty-plus-resort Magic Pass network.

other.label: Where the bottleneck actually is
other.text: Every route to the summit, the Laub, the Steinberg and the Galtiberg funnels through the Rotair, a single revolving cable car shared with non-skiing sightseers visiting the glacier attraction — arrive at opening on any Titlis-side day, since the queue compounds through the morning and does not meaningfully shorten until mid-afternoon.

proTips: Ride the first Titlis Xpress cabin of the day, every glacier-side day — the Rotair queue is driven as much by sightseers as by skiers, and it only gets longer after mid-morning.
Schedule the Laub and Steinberg earlier in the week and Brunni as the recovery day — both big descents are physically taxing and benefit from fresh legs.
Confirm the Galtiberg's exit transport (road pickup or the Stäfeli bus) with the guide the night before, not on the mountain — this route does not return to the lift network.
Use the Brunni pass, not the full destination pass, on the fallback day — no reason to pay for Rotair access you will not use.
Check the SLF bulletin before booking the Steinberg or Galtiberg — both cross genuinely crevassed or remote terrain and the guide will reorder the week around the forecast, not the itinerary.
Keep a spare unscheduled day loose if possible; Engelberg's best guided days are weather windows, not calendar dates.

packingNotes: Full avalanche kit: transceiver, probe, shovel, mandatory for every guided descent this week.
Wide freeride skis or a freeride splitboard; there is little reason to bring narrow piste skis for this trip.
A climbing harness may be requested by the guide for the Steinberg glacier approach — ask when booking.
A hardshell and warm midlayers; the Titlis summit at 3,020 m is routinely 15–20°C colder and windier than the village.
A day pack with room for skins (if the guide requests a short boot-pack or skin section) plus food and water for the long Galtiberg day.
Sturdy off-mountain boots for the Galtiberg's forest walk-out, which can be on unbroken snow.
whatCouldGoWrong: **The Rotair queue eats the morning.** Fallback: use the earlier orientation day to learn its rhythm, and always take the first cabin on a big-descent day rather than a mid-morning one.

**Titlis is wind-closed.** Fallback: Brunni's lower, more sheltered sector keeps the week skiable — this is a genuine plan B, not a consolation prize, and is scheduled into the week for exactly this reason.

**The Galtiberg is called off for crevasse or avalanche risk.** Fallback: the guide substitutes a shorter, better-secured glacier line off Titlis, or moves the day to Brunni and reschedules Galtiberg for later in the week if a weather window opens.

**Guided days are fully booked.** Fallback: book Outventure or a Bergführer before arrival; walking in to Engelberg without a pre-booked guide is the most common reason visiting freeriders miss the area's signature descents.
**A member of the group is not fit for the Galtiberg's full length.** Fallback: split the group — Outventure can run a shorter Steinberg repeat for anyone not up for the long exit.
